description:
DELETE-USER-SEC-FILE's WHEN DFHRESP(NOTFND) arm at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:323-328 - the MIDDLE of that EVALUATE's three arms, the only one of them that emits no DISPLAY, and the case that discharges gate G47 for the deleteHeld call site alongside case09 and case10 (NORMAL) and case11 (WHEN OTHER). PF5 takes the FOURTH arm of the ordered EVALUATE EIBAID at :108-130 - DFHENTER, DFHPF3, DFHPF4, DFHPF5, DFHPF12, WHEN OTHER, first match wins, no fall-through - into DELETE-USER-INFO at :174-192. USRIDINI is non-blank, so the EVALUATE TRUE at :176-186 falls to the WHEN OTHER of :183-185, which moves -1 into USRIDINL and then reaches a CONTINUE that does nothing and does NOT raise the error flag. The single IF NOT ERR-FLG-ON at :188 wraps BOTH the read at :190 and the delete at :191: there is NO second guard between them, unlike PROCESS-ENTER-KEY at :156-169 where two separate guards let a failed read suppress the repaint, and that structural difference is modelled here as it is written rather than as a guard that does not exist. This paragraph also never blanks FNAMEI, LNAMEI or USRTYPEI - the MOVE SPACES at :157-159 belongs to PROCESS-ENTER-KEY - so the three names the terminal transmitted survive untouched to the last send. READ-USER-SEC-FILE at :267-300 issues EXEC CICS READ ... UPDATE with RIDFLD(SEC-USR-ID) against USER0005, a key the seed genuinely holds, so its NORMAL arm at :281-286 runs: the dead CONTINUE at :282 is preserved rather than tidied, 'Press PF5 key to delete this user ...' goes to WS-MESSAGE at :283-284, DFHNEUTR goes to ERRMSGC at :285, and the screen is sent - send 1 of 2. SEC-USR-ID now holds USER0005 and the task HOLDS the record. DELETE-USER-SEC-FILE at :302-336 then issues EXEC CICS DELETE at :307-311 with DATASET, RESP and RESP2 and NO RIDFLD: it removes the record the preceding read-for-update left the task holding and never a record located by key, so the repository contract asserted here is readForUpdate then deleteHeld, and a translation reading delete(userId) would pass a naive test yet succeed where the COBOL cannot. THE DELETE REPORTS NOT FOUND. The outcome is forced as FileStatus.Outcome.NOT_FOUND with RESP 13 - common.FileStatus.NOTFND - and RESP2 0, common.FileStatus.NO_REASON_CODE, named by outcome rather than encoded as a bare number so the case and the repository agree on what is being forced, and forced because no arrangement of seeded rows can make a record vanish between the read at :190 and the delete at :191 within one task. The arm is genuinely reachable in the source because EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :313 tests the DELETE's own response, which the command sets independently of whatever the READ reported: the arm must therefore be driven even though a delete of a held record would not ordinarily report not-found. THREE THINGS DISTINGUISH THIS ARM FROM THE ONE BESIDE IT, and all three are asserted. First the text: :325-326 moves 'User ID NOT found...' into WS-MESSAGE - capital NOT, lower-case found, exactly three dots and no space before them - byte-identical to the literal the read's own not-found arm moves at :289-290 and therefore byte-identical to the message case07 pins, and NOT the 'Unable to Update User...' of :332-333. Second the cursor: :327 moves -1 into USRIDINL, the user-id field, where the WHEN OTHER arm at :334 moves it into FNAMEL instead; cursorField is USRIDINL and FNAMEL is not touched. Third the silence: there is NO DISPLAY statement on this arm. The DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD line appears at :294 and :330 only, both of them WHEN OTHER arms, so expectedMessages carries exactly TWO entries here where case11 carries three, and emitting a DISPLAY_LINE would be copying case11's arm by mistake. NOTHING IS BLANKED: INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS at :349-356 is performed only by the delete's NORMAL arm at :315 and by the PF4 clear at :343, never here, so USRIDINO still reads USER0005 and FNAMEO, LNAMEO and USRTYPEO still carry LEE, TING and U exactly as the RECEIVE delivered them. That is a real behavioural difference from case09 and case10, where the success arm empties the screen before painting its confirmation, and asserting blanks here would be wrong. ERRMSGC IS DERIVED, NOT GUESSED: this arm never touches the colour byte, so it retains the DFHNEUTR the read's NORMAL arm moved at :285 - not the DFHGREEN the delete-success arm moves at :317, and not the red the ERRMSG DFHMDF at app/bms/COUSR03.bms:140-143 bakes into the physical map, because :285 has already overwritten it on this path. Re-entry carrying an error is the state in which an error highlight applies, and COUSR03C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY, so the byte set inline is the whole of it; the mnemonic comes from common.BmsAttributes, which reproduces the absent IBM-supplied DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR from IBM CICS documentation, as common.CicsAid does for the DFHAID mnemonic DFHPF5 (risk R-D). TWO SENDS ARE PERFORMED AND THE COUNT IS BEHAVIOUR: SEND-USRDEL-SCREEN at :213-225 repaints all six header items through POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :243-262 on both, and only the last leaves the five variable items and the colour byte the terminal is left showing. THE IDENTIFIER IS USER0005, and the choice is deliberate. This case needs a key the seed genuinely carries so that the read really succeeds and the failure is isolated to the delete; USER0005 at seed index 9 - LEE, TING, type U - is exactly that, it is the identifier the gate's own operation trace for this case names, and ADMIN003 is the key case13 uses for the delete's DUPREC path, so reusing it here would blur two cases that must stay distinguishable. THE RETURN CODE IS 0 as a positive assertion rather than a default: COUSR03C contains zero CALL 'CEE3ABD' sites and never moves a severity into RETURN-CODE, so a delete that reports not-found does not abend. USRSEC IS UNCHANGED, which is what a refused delete means: expectedWrites is empty - a positive assertion that nothing was written, not an absence of interest - and ALL TEN rows are pinned at zero-based indices 0 through 9 with USER0005 still present at index 9, each by its six CSUSR01Y names and as its whole eighty-byte image. This is the direct counterpoint to case10, where the deleted row is gone. SEC-USR-FILLER is pinned BY NAME as twenty-three spaces, because 8 + 20 + 20 + 8 + 1 = 57 and only that filler carries the record to the 80 that RECORDSIZE(80,80) at app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:64-66 and LRECL=80 at :48 declare; a codec that omitted it would fail on the total width alone. The literal PASSWORD in SEC-USR-PWD is legacy sample data carried byte for byte because the copybook places it inside those eighty bytes - plaintext credentials are an inherited property of the legacy design rather than a choice made here, this screen has no password item among the eleven xxxI items COUSR03.CPY declares and never paints or reads that span, and no hashing, encoding or token is introduced. The dataset is addressed only by its binding key USRSEC and never by a dataset name. The communication area, the AID and the screen values travel in the payload alone - no server-side session state - in keeping with the pseudo-conversational contract, and the invocation ends at the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CU03') COMMAREA of :134-137, so the termination is RETURN_TRANSID and not an XCTL. NO USER RULES GOVERN THIS FILE: review_rules returns exactly 'No user rules provided.', which is the whole document; no rule has been invented and the absence is not treated as permission to lower the bar - the enterprise practices of the plan govern instead. PROVENANCE: every value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:302-336, specifically the NOTFND arm at :323-328, together with :106-137, :174-192, :213-225, :232-238, :243-262, :267-300 and :349-356, cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 for the six spans, app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY for the eleven xxxI items and the USRIDINL and FNAMEL length items, app/bms/COUSR03.bms for the field attributes, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy with app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:50-58 for the 194-byte area, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:18-22 for the two forty-character titles, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the header clock, app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy for the shared message structures, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:88-99 whose DELETE(YES) at :94 authorises this path, and the ten in-stream rows of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, with the clock pinned to the version footer at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:358 exactly as case01 pins it. It is NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL: running it is empirically impossible in this environment - no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler's indexed-file handler is disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository - which is the documented eight-blocker deviation escalated as risk R-A. It changes the provenance of the expected values and nothing else: the twenty cases, the field-by-field diffing and the zero-diff gate all stand.

THE OPERATION ORDER, DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED. expectedOperations names every USRSEC operation this case must issue, in order, and it is an assertion a byte fingerprint structurally cannot make: the EXEC CICS DELETE at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:307-311 names no RIDFLD, so it removes the record the task is HOLDING and is only ever correct after the EXEC CICS READ ... UPDATE at :269-278 took that hold on the same record. An empty list is equally an assertion - it says this path never reached the file at all.

THE FIRST SEND CARRIES THE WHOLE MAP AREA. EXEC CICS SEND MAP('COUSR3A') MAPSET('COUSR03') FROM(COUSR3AO) ERASE CURSOR at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:219-225 transmits the entire symbolic-map area, not the items the sending paragraph happened to touch, so all eleven xxxO items are on the wire at the first send exactly as they are at the last - and :217 moves WS-MESSAGE to ERRMSGO on every one of them. Because COUSR3AO REDEFINES COUSR3AI in app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY, the four writable items still hold precisely what the terminal sent: DELETE-USER-INFO at :174-192 - unlike PROCESS-ENTER-KEY at :156-159 and :164-166 - never moves SPACES over FNAMEI, LNAMEI and USRTYPEI and never re-populates them from the record, so USRIDINO, FNAMEO, LNAMEO and USRTYPEO echo this case's received mapFields padded to their declared PIC X widths. ERRMSGO and ERRMSGC on the first send are the DFHRESP(NORMAL) arm at :281-286, which moves DFHNEUTR to ERRMSGC before it sends. Pinning all eleven on sends[0] is what makes the two sends distinguishable rather than merely countable: the second differs from the first only in ERRMSGO, in ERRMSGC, and in whatever INITIALIZE-ALL-FIELDS at :349-355 cleared.
